# ICellRange.SetValuesOptions.arrayFixed

```ts
/**
 * Enter a single formula as an array formula (Excel's Ctrl+Shift+Enter) over the whole range.
 *
 * @defaultValue `false`
 *
 * @remarks
 * The range is the block's extent and the formula sits at its top-left; the result is fitted
 * to the extent rather than spilling from it - a dimension of 1 broadcasts, a longer one is
 * clipped, a shorter one is padded with `#N/A` - and the block never resizes. Its cells can
 * only be changed as a whole: overwriting, clearing, or inserting/deleting through part of a
 * block is refused ("You can't change part of an array"); rewriting it through this option
 * with the same range replaces it.
 *
 * Only meaningful for {@link ICellRange.setFormula} with one formula.
 */
arrayFixed?: boolean;
```

/**
 * Set the value(s) of one or more cells within a range.
 *
 * @param values The value to be set or a callback that will generate a value.
 * @returns The current `ICellRange`.
 *
 * @remarks
 * - `null` values will clear the corresponding cells.
 * - `undefined` values will be ignored, leaving the existing cell values unchanged.
 * - The array is row-major. An array smaller than the range writes only the cells it covers.
 * - A single value is {@link setValue}, which fills the range with it.
